CruiseMapper currently has no ship schedule for Port Aliaga Ship Breaking Yard (Turkey)

Aliaga (port locode TRALI) is an Eastern Mediterranean/Aegean Sea port town in Turkey's Izmir Province, with population around 60,000. Aliaga is approx 50 km (31 mi) north of the province's capital Izmir.

Port Aliaga (locode TRALI) serves mainly oil tankers and bulk cargo ships. The region's economy is based on tourism, shipbreaking, crude oil processing (petroleum refinery).

Aliaga Ship Breaking Yard houses several facilities used for dismantling and scrapping of mainly passenger ships (ferries and cruise liners). The cruise shipbreaking increased due to the Coronavirus crisis, and especially in 2020-2021, when shipowners sold for scrap some of their fleets' oldest vessels that were idled/in cold layups and losing money.

By capacity and annual scrapped DWT-deadweight tonnage, Aliaga is currently ranked the world's fourth-largest shipbreaking facility - following Alang (India), Chittagong (Bangladesh) and Gadani (Pakistan).

Currently awaiting with a most uncertain future (located in Greece, "close to Aliaga" and awaiting scrapping) are the passenger ships Marella Celebration (1984), Pullmantur Horizon (1990), Pullmantur Zenith (1992), Majesty of the Seas (1992).

The list of the scrapped ship's former owners includes Carnival Corporation (via the subsidiaries CCL-Carnival, Costa, Princess), Royal Caribbean Group (via Pullmantur, RCI-Royal Caribbean International), NCLH (via NCL-Norwegian Cruise Line), Fred Olsen, CMV-Cruise and Maritime Voyages (2010-founded/2020-defunct), Portuscale Cruises (2013-founded/2021-defunct), Epirotiki Line (1850-founded/2005-defunct).

Note: Due to the Coronavirus crisis and IMO's new regulations (marine engine upgrades for using low-sulfur fuels and LNG), in 2020-2021 were scrapped 15 cruise liners - an unprecedented number in comparison to previous years, and even 5-year periods. In 2020, the average ship scrap metal (DWT-deadweight tonnage) prices in Alang rose to ~USD 400 per ton (from ~$200), in Aliaga - to ~USD 300 per ton (from ~$100). EU-flagged ships' scrap values were ~USD 100-200 per ton as these vessels require dismantling at EU-certified yards. Ship scrap prices in the USA were USD 80-90 per ton.

Not a Cruise Passenger Port

Independent sightseeing is not possible. Aliağa Ship Breaking Yard is an active industrial ship-recycling area rather than a cruise terminal. Passenger ships listed here normally arrive at the end of their service lives for dismantling, not on scheduled cruise calls.

There is no cruise terminal, tender landing, shuttle service or authorized passenger exit associated with the ship-breaking yard. The recycling facilities are controlled workplaces with heavy machinery and significant safety hazards. Visitors should not attempt to enter the yards or approach them on foot.

What the Schedule Means

Arrivals shown for this location generally record vessels being delivered for recycling. They should not be interpreted as opportunities to embark, disembark or visit Aliağa during a cruise.

Because this is not a passenger port of call, self-guided walking tours, beaches and shore excursions are not applicable. Travelers visiting the wider Aliağa area independently should arrange their plans from the town itself and remain outside restricted port and industrial zones.
